trial_title: Testogel® (Testosterone Gel 50mg/5g) in the Treatment of Male Hypogonadism
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Testogel® 50mg/5g gel administered once daily (QD, morning dosing) compared to placebo administered once daily (QD, morning dosing), for 3 months, in hypogonadal men with testosterone deficiency being confirmed by clinical features and biochemical tests. For men with hypogonadism, treatment aims to restore testosterone levels to normal physiological range.

eligibility_table.criterion: Male ages 18-68 years diagnosed as having testosterone deficiency with clinical symptoms
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is 19 years old, male, and has testosterone deficiency with clinical symptoms such as delayed puberty and hypogonadism.

eligibility_table.criterion: A morning (8:00-10:00) serum Total Testosterone concentration of ≤ 300 ng/dL, confirmed by a second measurement of morning serum Total Testosterone concentration ≤ 300 ng/dL (samples to be taken 1 - 3 weeks apart)
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's morning serum Total Testosterone concentration ≤ 300 ng/dL confirmed by a second measurement taken 1 - 3 weeks apart?

eligibility_table.criterion: Abnormal prostate as evidenced by prostatic symptoms, prostatic masses or induration on rectal examination, or elevated levels of prostate specific antigen (PSA > 4ng/ml) or a maximum urine flow rate of less than 12 ml/sec(of a urine volume greater than 150ml) (and/or an International Prostate Symptom Score IPSS score >19)
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of abnormal prostate symptoms or elevated PSA levels in the patient's profile.
